body_markdown:

title: Millenium Development Goals
body_markdown:
(a) Study Fig 1.1, which shows the Millennium Development Goals.
(i) Explain what is meant by the following terms: gender equality and universal primary education.[2]
(ii) Goal 1 was to 'eradicate extreme poverty and hunger'.
 State two indicators which could be used to measure poverty and hunger.[2]. 
(iii) Goal 6 was to 'combat HIVIAIDS, malaria and other diseases' .
 Explain why it is important to reduce the amount of people suffering from diseases in developing countries.[3]. 
(b) Study Fig 1.2, which shows the results of a survey on the success of the Millennium Development Goals.
 700 people from different parts of the world were asked the following question. 'How successful do you think the Millennium Development Goals have been?' 
 Complete the bar for Millennium Development Goal 1 by plotting the following information.[3] 
 Successful (18% ) 
 Not successful (52% ) 
 Do not know (30%).
 Using Fig 1.2, put the following goals in rank order according to how successful people think they have been. You should rank the goals from most successful to least successful.
(iii) Using Fig 1.2, compare the opinions of the people interviewed about the success of Millennium Development Goals 3 and 6.
 You should use statistics in your answer[3]
(iv) Suggest two reasons for the difference in opinions of the people surveyed about the success of the Millennium Development Goals.
 For each reason you should explain your answer.[4]. 
(c) Study Table 1.3, which shows how successful the Millennium Development Goals have been in different parts of Asia.
(i) Identify the following:
 a Millennium Development Goal which has been partly successful in three parts of Asia.
 a Millennium Development Goal which has been unsuccessful in two parts of Asia.[2] 
 Compare the success of the Millennium Development Goals in Eastern Asia and Western Asia.
 Refer to evidence from Table 1.3 in your answer.[4]

title: Bangladesh Clothing Industry
body_markdown:
2
(a) Study the information below: which shows a newspaper report about the clothing industry of Bangladesh.
 Bangladesh is one of the world's largest exporters of garments (clothing), mainly shirts. Almost 80% of its exports are garments, with a value of around USS25 billion. They are the biggest earner of foreign currency. The industry employs over 4 million people, mainly women.
 Although Bangladesh grows some of the cotton it needs, much of it is imported from the USA, India and Pakistan. Textiles and chemicals, such as dyes, are also imported in large quantities.
 The  industry has strong competition from Thailand and China in particular and the development of new products is important if Bangladesh is to keep its share of the market in the world of fashion. It also needs to look for other markets as well as North America and Europe.
Another challenge for the industry is to ensure safe working conditions, as many workers have died in accidents in garment factories. A reliable supply of cheap energy is also essential if the industry is to remain a major contributor to the country's GDP.
(i) What proportion of the exports of Bangladesh are garments?[1] 
(ii) Where are the main markets for garments made in Bangladesh?[1] 
(iii) Identify three inputs of the garment industry stated in Fig: 2.1.[3]. (b) Explain what is meant by the following terms:
 intermediate technology[2]
 economies of scale.[2] 
(c) Some industries try to make their production as sustainable as possible.
 Explain methods that could be used to limit environmental destruction and exploitation of local communities.[5].
(d) Explain how industrialisation contributes to the development of a country.
 You should develop fully the points you make.[6]

title: Infant Mortality
body_markdown:
(a) Study the segment below, which shows information about a research investigation conducted in Ondo State , Nigeria, a developing country in Sub-Saharan Africa.
 The researchers wanted to find out why infant mortality was high in the area. A questionnaire was written and it was given to 20 mothers in a pilot study, who were asked to return it to the researchers when they had completed it.
 In the main study a sample of 210 mothers of babies who were less than one year old was used: The researchers decided that they would complete the questionnaire face-to- face with the mothers, rather than leaving it for them to complete as they had done in the pilot study.
(i) What was the aim of the research described in Fig: 3.1? 
(ii) Suggest two reasons why these researchers conducted a pilot study.[2]
(iii) Suggest reasons why the researchers decided to complete the questionnaire face-to- face with the mothers, rather than leaving it for them to complete and return.[4]. 
(iv) The 210 people who were selected to complete the questionnaire could have been selected using a random sample, a systematic sample or a stratified sample.
 Which type of sample do you think would have been best? Justify your choice.[2]
 State one other source of primary data and one source of secondary data which the researchers could have used in this study.[2]
(vi) Give two reasons why secondary data is not always reliable.[2]. 
(b) Study Fig 3.2 , which is a question taken from the survey conducted in Ondo State, Nigeria: For each of the following do you think this is a cause of babies dying in their first year?
 Fig 3.3 shows the results of the answers from the 210 mothers. 
(i) Complete Fig 3.3 by plotting the following information.[3] 
 Lack of medical care = 25%
 Agree  Disagree = 35% 
 Do not know = 40% 
(ii) What conclusions can be made from the information plotted in Fig. 3.3? Refer to statistics in your answer.[4]

title: Informal Settlements
body_markdown:
(a) Study Figs. 3.1 and 3.2 , which show parts of a squatter settlement in Mumbai, India.
(i) A group of three students of Development Studies was planning a research investigation in this squatter settlement where approximately 1000 people were living. Firstly they visited the area to make observations.
Describe observations they could have made about:
 the location of the homes shown in Fig: 3.1
 the features of the homes shown in Fig: 3.2.[4] 
(ii) Suggest three practical difficulties of collecting data in a squatter settlement.[3].
(b) The students decided to investigate the following research questions.
 Research question 1: Have most people migrated to Mumbai for employment?
 Research question 2: Are there more advantages than difficulties for people living in the squatter settlement?
(i) The students decided to use a questionnaire. Before they visited the squatter settlement they carried out a pilot study in a housing area close to their school.
 State two advantages of carrying out a pilot study.[2]
(ii) When the students had completed their pilot study they had to agree on a suitable number of people to answer their questionnaire. One student suggested a sample of 15 people; another suggested 300 people.
 Explain why:
 a sample of 15 people is too small
 a sample of 300 people is too big[2]. 
(iii) The teacher advised the students to sample 50 households:
 Name and describe a sampling method which they could have used to choose the 50 households to visit to complete the questionnaire. Explain why you have chosen this method.[3] 
(c) The questionnaire used by the students asked four questions.
(i) Use the results of question 2 to complete the pie chart.[2].
(ii) The results of questions 3 and 4 in the questionnaire are shown in the tables below.
 Suggest why using bar graphs would be an appropriate method to present this data, rather than using line graphs or pie charts.[3]. 
(iii) Two of the problems suggested by people who live in the squatter settlement were 'flooding' and 'fire'.
 Using Figs. 3.1 and 3.2, suggest why these are problems in the squatter settlement.[4].
(iv) What conclusions do you think the students reached about the research questions which they were investigating? Support your answers with data from the tables on pages 15 and 17 .
 Research question 1: 
 Have most people migrated to Mumbai for employment?[3]
 Research question 2: 
 Are there more advantages than difficulties for people living in the squatter settlement?[4]. 
(d) Suggest how the investigation could be extended by investigating the problem of water pollution in and around the squatter settlement.
 You should refer to both primary and secondary methods which could be used to collect data.[7]
